1.why: Verify-token only accepts a recovery owned by the current session and matches the submitted token against that recovery’s SHA-256 hash.

2.why: Tokens are bound to a single session-scoped recovery via ownedRecovery and tokenHash, so the same code cannot authorize a different session/user.

3.why: Password reset only sets recovery.passwordHash and never invalidates or deletes other entries in the sessions map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key only and HSTS is set, though the exact TLS version is left to Bun defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and new passwords via Bun.password.hash bcrypt cost 12; no reversible encryption of tokens is used.

6.why: No real email is sent; the API returns mockToken in JSON and the UI/logs display it, so private reset material is not guarded in a message channel.

7.why: Inputs are length-limited and validated, passwords cleared after hashing, and the SPA inserts dynamic values only with textContent.

8.why: Navigation uses only same-origin hash routes from a fixed allowlist; no open external redirects exist.

9.why: There are no server email templates that embed user input as HTML or scripts.

10.why: Demo recovery logs and UI intentionally surface the mock reset token and MFA code; errors are generic but tokens still appear in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed at runtime, but the MFA secret MFA_CODE is hardcoded in source as "246810".

12.why: There are no login default users/passwords, but the fixed demo MFA code acts as a known default credential.

13.why: Per-recovery attempt counters with temporary blocks and separate IP rate limits reject repeated failed token/MFA/password tries.

14.why: /api/recovery always returns the same generic success path and ignores whether the email is valid or registered.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte crypto.getRandomValues hex values, hashed at rest, single-use, TTL-limited, and tied to one recovery/session.
